stories.title: Spanish transport minister resigns after two deadly train crashes in one year
stories.description: Spain’s Minister of Transport Óscar Puente announced his resignation after two deadly train crashes occurred in a single year, including one last week that killed 69 people.
stories.excerpt: Spain’s Minister of Transport Óscar Puente announced his resignation after two deadly train crashes occurred in a single year, including one last week that killed 69 people. “I made the decision about my future in the first few minutes after the tragedy,” Puente told lawmakers in Madrid. “A transport minister in a country like Spain cannot remain in office after two accidents of this severity in less than a year, however different they may be and regardless of whether or not they bear direct responsibility for them.” Puente’s announcement arrives just three weeks before the country’s general elections, which the minister said he would not be standing as a candidate. His resignation comes six days after two high-speed trains collided after what authorities say was a combination of human and computer errors. One train, operated by Spain’s national rail service, crashed into a stationary train at high speed, despite a safety system shutdown that had halted all rail traffic along the line.
